about.title: Escondido Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Escondido sits inland in North San Diego County, and its roads carry the daily traffic of roughly 151,000 residents plus everyone moving through on I-15. In 2025, public records show 896 injury collisions in the city, with 1,297 people hurt and 10 lives lost. Valley Parkway, Washington Avenue and Mission Avenue appear most often in those reports, and the counts tend to rise on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. as the workweek ends. If one of those crashes was yours, the days afterward can feel like a second collision: adjusters calling, a car that won't start, medical bills you never planned for. LawProactive is here to take one item off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Escondido car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened, we make the introduction, and you decide whether that attorney is the right fit.

whyChoose.title: Why Escondido Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock in California is real
items.desc: Most car accident claims here must be filed within two years, but if a city vehicle, Caltrans truck or other government party was involved, a claim may need to be filed in as little as six months. The attorney we connect you with can pin down which deadline applies to you.

items.title: Being partly at fault doesn't end your claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you shared some blame at that Mission Avenue intersection, you can still recover, reduced by your percentage of responsibility. Insurers know this and may push a higher share onto you than the evidence supports.

items.title: Protect your evidence before the other insurer calls
items.desc: Photos, dashcam footage, witness contacts and your medical records matter more the earlier they're preserved. You are not required to give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement, and an attorney can handle those conversations for you.

items.question: My crash happened on I-15 in Escondido. Does that change anything about my claim?
items.answer: The location matters mainly for who investigated and who may be responsible. A freeway collision is typically handled by the California Highway Patrol rather than Escondido police, so your report will come from a different agency. If a road condition or a government vehicle contributed, the shortened six-month government claim window could apply, which is one reason to speak with an attorney early.

items.question: The other driver's insurer wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You aren't obligated to, and most attorneys will advise against it. Recorded statements are often used to lock you into an early version of events before you know the full extent of your injuries. Cooperate with your own insurer as your policy requires, but let an attorney manage contact with the other side.

items.question: What does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we don't charge you for the introduction. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there is no attorney fee unless your case results in a recovery, and there is no obligation to hire the attorney we connect you with.
